title: Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: Onboarding and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines the standard process for creating prompt sets, running benchmark suites, onboarding new models into the eval harness, applying quantization profiles for cost/performance tradeoffs, and performing regression triage when metrics degrade. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and SREs responsible for model quality and inference economics.

Scope:
- Applies to all model onboarding activities for Redwood-hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Covers prompt-set creation, benchmark jobs, acceptance criteria, quantization smoke tests, and regression triage workflows.
- Does not replace per-customer privacy/PII reviews; see security-and-compliance pages for that process.

Key Definitions:
- Prompt set: curated input examples representing a workload (user queries, system prompts, edge cases).
- Benchmark run: an automated job that evaluates model outputs against metrics defined for a prompt set.
- Regression: a statistically significant degradation in one or more guardrail metrics compared to baseline.

Owners and Roles

- Model Owner: owns onboarding checklist, prompt sets, and accepts model into serving.
- Eval Owner: schedules benchmark jobs, maintains harness configurations.
- Applied ML Lead: triage owner for quality regressions.
- SRE/Platform: owns infra for large-scale benchmark execution and production rollout automation.

Process: Onboarding a Model (high level)

1. Prepare artifacts (Model Owner)
   - Model binary and manifest (architecture, tokenizer, HF or internal artifact ID).
   - Initial performance profile: expected latency, peak tokens/sec, and target quantization variants.
   - Suggested prompt sets: at minimum "sanity", "smoke", "core-product", "adversarial".

2. Create prompt sets (Model Owner + Applied ML)
   - Use the prompt template: metadata, intent tags, expected labels (if applicable), input, and optional canonical answer.
   - Include distributional metadata: length histogram, language, domain.
   - Minimum sizes: sanity (10), smoke (100), core-product (>=1k representative samples), adversarial (50 targeted examples).

3. Define benchmark configs (Eval Owner)
   - Metrics: Exact Match (where applicable), BLEU/ROUGE for structured text, Rouge-L for long form, Semantic Similarity (embedding cosine), Safety flags (binary), Hallucination rate (custom detectors), Latency P50/P95, Cost per 1k tokens.
   - Acceptance thresholds (example):
     - Core-product: semantic_similarity >= 0.80 (median) and hallucination_rate <= 2%
     - Safety: critical_safety_violations == 0 on safety-critical prompt set
     - Latency: P95 <= 450ms for hosted-1k token workload

4. Run baseline benchmark (Eval Owner)
   - Execute against the chosen baseline model/tag and the new model.
   - Record outputs, embeddings, logs, and token-level timing.
   - Store run metadata in eval-harness (job id, model_tag, commit, config).

5. Review and acceptance (Model Owner + Applied ML)
   - If all acceptance thresholds pass, schedule a canary serving rollout per rollout playbook.
   - If minor fails (one-off cases), create remediation plan and iterate.

Prompt Set Guidelines

- Structure: JSONL with fields: id, split (train/val/smoke), input, expected (optional), tags, source, length_tokens, notes.
- Tag taxonomy: product_area, intent, language, complexity, safety_risk (low/medium/high).
- Maintain one canonical prompt-set repository in eval-harness with versioning.

Example prompt JSONL record (single line):
{
  "id": "core-0001",
  "split": "val",
  "input": "Summarize the following user message in two sentences:
...",
  "expected": "Two-sentence concise summary",
  "tags": ["summarization", "customer-support"],
  "length_tokens": "120"
}

Benchmark Job Templates and CLI

- CI job: eval/bench/run-batch --model model_tag --prompt-set core-product --metrics semantic_similarity,hallucination,latency --out run-<date>-<model>.tar.gz
- Quick local smoke: python harness/run_eval.py --config configs/smoke.yaml --model path/to/model --prompts prompts/smoke.jsonl

Quantization Profiles and Smoke Tests

- Profiles: fp16, int8-dynamic, int8-static (recommended profiles stored in quantization-profiles/).
- Smoke test checklist for each profile:
  1. Model loads without OOM on target instance type.
  2. Generate 50-sample smoke prompt set and compare semantic_similarity delta vs fp16 baseline (delta <= 0.03).
  3. Validate safety detector outputs unchanged (no increase in critical violations).
  4. Record throughput gain and cost estimate.

Regression Detection and Alerting

- Guardrail metrics to monitor: semantic_similarity_p50/p95, hallucination_rate, safety_critical_count, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - semantic_similarity_p50 drop >= 0.05 from baseline -> SEV-2 alert
  - hallucination_rate increase >= 1 percentage point and absolute > 3% -> SEV-2
  - safety_critical_count > 0 -> SEV-1 immediate pager

Triage Playbook (when a regression alert fires)

1. Acknowledge & Triage lead assigned (Applied ML Lead)
2. Gather signals (first 30 minutes)
   - Latest benchmark run id and baseline id.
   - Model artifact id (git commit or model registry tag).
   - Prompt-set split and recent traffic samples that triggered alert.
   - System metrics: throttling, timeouts, quantization profile in use, hardware type.
3. Reproduce locally and in harness (first 2 hours)
   - Re-run benchmark with archived run config and seeds.
   - Compare token-level diffs and embedding similarity distribution.
4. Classify root cause (by 4 hours):
   - Model regression (new weights or tokenization change).
   - Prompt-set distribution shift (incoming traffic differs).
   - Infra/serving degradation (timeouts, failed KV-cache).
   - Quantization-induced error.
5. Mitigation examples:
   - Immediate rollback to previous model tag (if model regression) and open bug for model team.
   - If distribution shift: add new prompt examples to core-product and update thresholds.
   - If quantization: fall back to higher-precision profile for affected route.
6. Postmortem & Preventative Work (within 5 business days)
   - Postmortem with timeline, root cause, action items, owner, and due dates.
   - Update eval harness to add failing prompts to nightly smoke tests.

Acceptance Criteria and SLOs for Eval Harness

- Nightly runs: complete within 4 hours for a standard core-product set (1k examples).
- Coverage: at least 80% of active routes must have a matched prompt set.
- Regression false-positive rate (alerts not actionable) < 10% monthly.

Templates and Artifacts (where to find)

- Prompt-set template: eval-harness/prompt-templates/canonical-prompt-template.jsonl
- Benchmark config examples: eval-harness/configs/core-product.yaml
- Quantization profiles: applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/README.md
- Regression runbook: applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/triage-runbook.md

Related pages

- eval-harness standards and onboarding guide (see related_pages).
- Quality guardrails and safety detectors.

Appendix: Example benchmark config (YAML)

metrics:
  - semantic_similarity:
      embedding_model: "rwd-embed-qa-128"
      threshold: 0.80
  - hallucination_rate:
      detector: "internal-hallucination-detector-v2"
  - latency:
      p95_threshold_ms: 450

Notes on reproducibility

- Always pin tokenizer and model artifact ids in benchmark metadata.
- Store raw outputs alongside parsed metrics to support token-level diffing.
- When adding new prompt sets, include a short provenance note (source, author, collection date).

Contact

For questions or to request a prompt-set review, contact the Applied ML team at applied-ml@redwood.ai or the eval-harness owner via internal slack #eval-harness.
